english.title: Use another to look after / hide / transport a firearm - Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), to look after, hide or transport a dangerous weapon, being a firearm, namely **(..DESCRIBE THE FIREARM..), for you under arrangements or in circumstances that facilitated, or were intended to facilitate, the firearm being available to you for an unlawful purpose
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 28 and 29 of the Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
used another person to look after / hide / transport a firearm for you
under arrangements OR
in circumstances that facilitate / that were intended to facilitate
that firearm being available to you for an unlawful purpose

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 28(2) provides interpretation of 'available for an unlawful purpose', and section 28(3) defines 'dangerous weapon'.
(ii) Children - where this offence was committed by an adult using a minor to look after, hide or transport the weapon this fact must be treated as an aggravating factor in sentencing, see section 70 of the Sentencing Act 2020.

other.penalty:
Indictment only - Ten years imprisonment and/or a fine. Where at the time of the offence, the offender was aged 16 or over, and the dangerous weapon in respect of which the offence was committed was a firearm mentioned in section 5(1)(a) to (af) or (c) or section 5(1A)(a) of the 1968 Act.

Where at the time of conviction the offender is aged under 18, in accordance with sections 249 and 250 of the Sentencing Act 2020 a sentence of detention under section 250 requiring the offender to be detained for the period specified in the sentence, is available.

A minimum sentence may apply to this offence, see section 311 of, and Schedule 20 to, the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
